q:
In the diagram, the lines QR and ST are parallel to each other. The shortest distance between these two lines is half the shortest distance between the point P and line QR. What is the ratio of the area of the triangle PST to the area of the trapezium SQRT?
Note: The figure shown is representative.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 200" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><polygon points="150,15 50,175 250,175" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="90" y1="95" x2="210" y2="95" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="146" y="12" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">P</text><text x="78" y="93" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">S</text><text x="214" y="93" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">T</text><text x="38" y="188" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">Q</text><text x="252" y="188" font-size="12" fill="currentColor">R</text></svg>
explanation: Since the P-to-ST distance equals the ST-to-QR distance, ST is the mid-segment of triangle PQR, so triangle PST is similar to PQR with linear ratio 1/2 and area ratio 1/4. The trapezium SQRT then has area 3/4 of PQR, giving area(PST):area(SQRT) = (1/4):(3/4) = 1/3.

options: None of the nodes will split.
At least one node will split and redistribute.
The total number of nodes will remain same.
The height of the tree will increase.
explanation: 23 belongs in the rightmost leaf [20,21,22], which is already full (3 keys), so it must split, promoting a new key to the root. The root is also already full with 3 keys, so it splits too, adding a new root level and increasing the tree's height. Hence a split occurs and the height increases, while the node count does not stay the same.

options: E3
E1
E2

q: Consider the following deterministic finite automaton (DFA) defined over the alphabet Σ = {a, b}. Identify which of the following language(s) is/are accepted by the given DFA.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 420 190" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah2025cs50" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><line x1="10" y1="95" x2="45" y2="95" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><circle cx="70" cy="95" r="22"/><circle cx="170" cy="95" r="22"/><circle cx="270" cy="95" r="22"/><circle cx="370" cy="95" r="22"/><circle cx="370" cy="95" r="17"/><path d="M60,75 A16,16 0 1 1 80,75" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><path d="M160,75 A16,16 0 1 1 180,75" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><line x1="92" y1="95" x2="148" y2="95" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><line x1="192" y1="95" x2="248" y2="95" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><line x1="292" y1="95" x2="348" y2="95" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><path d="M195,70 Q270,20 350,78" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><path d="M255,120 Q220,170 90,105" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/><path d="M355,110 Q290,175 185,108" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs50)"/></g><g font-size="13" fill="currentColor"><text x="64" y="100">q0</text><text x="164" y="100">q1</text><text x="264" y="100">q2</text><text x="364" y="100">q3</text><text x="66" y="45">a</text><text x="166" y="45">b</text><text x="115" y="88">b</text><text x="215" y="88">a</text><text x="315" y="88">b</text><text x="255" y="45">a</text><text x="165" y="150">a</text><text x="270" y="160">b</text></g></svg>
options: The set of all strings containing an even number of b's.
The set of all strings containing the pattern bab.
The set of all strings ending with the pattern bab.
The set of all strings not containing the pattern aba.
explanation: The DFA is the standard suffix-tracking automaton for 'bab': q0=no useful suffix matched, q1=suffix 'b' matched, q2=suffix 'ba' matched, q3 (accepting)=suffix 'bab' matched, and its transitions correctly re-sync on overlaps (e.g. q3 on 'a' goes back to q2, since 'aba's suffix 'a' is not a prefix match but the run continues correctly for further 'b's). It accepts exactly the strings ending in bab, not merely containing it.

q: A computer has a memory hierarchy consisting of two-level cache (L1 and L2) and a main memory. If the processor needs to access data from memory, it first looks into L1 cache. If the data is not found in L1 cache, it goes to L2 cache. If it fails to get the data from L2 cache, it goes to main memory, where the data is definitely available. Hit rates and access times of various memory units are shown in the figure. The average memory access time in nanoseconds (ns) is ________. (rounded off to two decimal places)
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 260" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah2025cs53" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><rect x="110" y="10" width="120" height="28"/><rect x="70" y="70" width="200" height="42"/><rect x="40" y="145" width="260" height="50"/><rect x="10" y="228" width="320" height="26"/><line x1="170" y1="38" x2="170" y2="65" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs53)"/><line x1="170" y1="112" x2="170" y2="140" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs53)"/><line x1="170" y1="195" x2="170" y2="223" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs53)"/></g><g font-size="10" fill="currentColor"><text x="148" y="28">Processor</text><text x="130" y="85">L1 cache</text><text x="120" y="98">Hit rate = 95%,</text><text x="105" y="110">Access time = 10 ns</text><text x="130" y="160">L2 cache</text><text x="55" y="173">Hit rate = 85%, access time</text><text x="55" y="185">(incl. L1 miss penalty) = 20 ns</text><text x="95" y="242">Main Memory: access time (incl.</text><text x="60" y="252">L1 & L2 miss penalty) = 200 ns</text></g></svg>
explanation: AMAT = 0.95×10 + 0.05×(0.85×20 + 0.15×200) = 9.5 + 0.05×(17+30) = 9.5 + 2.35 = 11.85 ns, since the L2 and main-memory access times already include the penalty of the level(s) above them.

q:
Consider the following database tables of a sports league.
player(pid, pname, age)          team(tid, tname, city, cid)
coach(cid, cname)                members(pid, tid)

An instance of the tables:
player: (1,Jasprit,31) (2,Atharva,24) (3,Ishan,26) (4,Axar,30)
coach: (101,Ricky) (102,Mark) (103,Trevor)
team: (10,MI,Mumbai,102) (20,DC,Delhi,101) (30,PK,Mohali,103)
members: (1,10) (2,30) (3,10) (4,20)

SELECT MIN(P.age)
FROM player P
WHERE P.pid IN (
    SELECT M.pid
    FROM team T, coach C, members M
    WHERE C.cname = 'Mark'
        AND T.cid = C.cid
        AND M.tid = T.tid
)

The value returned by the given SQL query is ________. (Answer in integer)
explanation: Coach Mark has cid=102, whose team is tid=10 (MI). Members of team 10 are pid 1 and 3, i.e. players Jasprit (31) and Ishan (26). MIN(age) over {31,26} is 26.

q: Suppose a message of size 15000 bytes is transmitted from a source to a destination using IPv4 protocol via two routers as shown in the figure. Each router has a defined maximum transmission unit (MTU) as shown in the figure, including IP header. The number of fragments that will be delivered to the destination is ________. (Answer in integer)
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 160" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah2025cs57" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" refX="6" refY="3.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.5 L0,7 Z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="40"/><rect x="310" y="10" width="80" height="40"/><rect x="120" y="70" width="90" height="40"/><rect x="240" y="70" width="90" height="40"/><line x1="30" y1="90" x2="115" y2="90" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs57)"/><line x1="210" y1="90" x2="235" y2="90" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs57)"/><path d="M350,70 L350,50" marker-end="url(#ah2025cs57)"/><path d="M285,70 L285,50 L350,50" fill="none"/></g><g font-size="10" fill="currentColor"><text x="25" y="34">Source</text><text x="322" y="34">Destination</text><text x="132" y="88">Router-1</text><text x="122" y="100">(MTU=5000 bytes)</text><text x="252" y="88">Router-2</text><text x="245" y="100">(MTU=3000 bytes)</text></g></svg>
explanation: At Router-1 (MTU 5000, 20-byte header ⇒ 4980-byte payload, offsets multiple of 8) the 14980-byte payload splits into fragments of 4976+4976+4976+52 bytes (4 fragments of total size 5000,5000,5000,72). At Router-2 (MTU 3000 ⇒ 2980-byte usable, offset-aligned to 2976) each of the first three (4980-byte payload) fragments needs 2 further fragments, while the 72-byte fragment needs none: 3×2+1 = 7 fragments reach the destination.

q: Consider the given sequential circuit designed using D-Flip-flops (D0-D3 feed Q0-Q3, connected in series Q0→D1, Q1→D2, Q2→D3, and the complemented output Q3' feeds back into D0). The circuit is initialized with some value (initial state). The number of distinct states the circuit will go through before returning back to the initial state is ________. (Answer in integer)
explanation: This is a 4-bit twisted-ring (Johnson) counter: D0 = Q3'. For a non-degenerate initial state it cycles through 2×4 = 8 distinct states before returning to the start (the key accepts 7 or 8 depending on whether the initial state itself is counted).

q: The maximum value of x such that the edge between the nodes B and C is included in every minimum spanning tree of the given graph is ________. (Answer in integer)

explanation: Removing edge BC, the minimum bottleneck path between B and C uses edges DB(3) and AD(6) and AC(1), whose maximum weight is 6. Edge BC is in every MST only while x is strictly less than this bottleneck value 6, so the largest integer x for which BC is guaranteed to be included is 5.
